job_description:
AI Specialist

Department: Academic Affairs

Location: Remote with two weeks of travel per year to
Columbia, MO

Type: Staff

Term: Full-time

Pay: $75,000-$85,000 per year (Pay range may vary based on
geographic location and years of experience)

Diversity Statement:

Columbia College is committed to creating an inclusive employee
experience for all regardless of race, color, national origin,
gender, religion, sexual orientation, age or disability. The
college maintains a safe place for open discourse; supports
activities that promote diversity and inclusion; and overall,
fosters a sense of community that welcomes everyone.

Job Summary:

Columbia College invites applications for a full-time AI Specialist
position with a start date of Fall 2024. Salary will be
commensurate with qualifications and experience. This position will
be part of the Academic Affairs department and report directly to
the Provost. This position will be responsible for: 1) developing
and conducting workshops, training sessions and events on AI
technologies for various college stakeholders; 2) training all
faculty regardless of modality on incorporating AI into teaching,
modeling what should be done in the classroom, and best practices
for AI use; and 3) collaboration with the following departments
frequently to advocate for innovative AI solutions that can benefit
the college: a) online instructional design team to ensure courses
are designed so that students are AI literate and how to utilize AI
tools to generate accommodations; b) Technology Services to ensure
the institution has the resources to stay ahead of the
ever-changing AI world, and software to ensure AI can be fully
utilized; and other duties as assigned.

This is a full-time position. Strong interpersonal skills,
cross-cultural sensitivity, and demonstrated potential to
contribute positively to the College community are expected.

Founded in 1851, Columbia College has been helping students advance
their lives through higher education for more than 160 years. A
private, nonprofit liberal arts and sciences college, Columbia
College takes pride in small classes, experienced faculty and
quality educational programs. Originally founded as Christian
Female College, the college changed its name to Columbia College In
1970. That year, it transitioned from a two-year women's college to
a four-year coeducational college.

Qualifications:

A candidate should have work experience in AI development,
applications, and proficiency in a variety of areas such as a)
Python, R, Java, C++, or other relevant programming languages; b)
Machine Learning Frameworks and Libraries, TensorFlow, PyTorch,
Keras, and scikit-learn; c) SQL, NoSQL databases, data cleaning,
and preprocessing; d) Familiarity with version control systems
(e.g., Git), integrated development environments (IDEs), and
containerization tools (ex. Docker); or e) Knowledge of cloud
platforms like AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure for deploying and
managing AI solutions. Preference will be given to a candidate who
has the above work experience in a higher education setting
training multiple stakeholders in AI use. A candidate should have
high ability in problem solving, strong analytical skills to
address complex issues, courage to take calculated risks, and
exceptional presentation skills with the ability to communicate
technical concepts to a wide variety of stakeholders, many of which
may not have a technical background. A Bachelor’s degree is
required, but a Master’s degree is preferred, in Computer Science,
AI, Data Science, Machine Learning or a related field.

To Apply:

The position will remain open until filled. Columbia College is an
equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from
underrepresented groups.

To be considered, submit applications online at ccis.edu/jobs.

Project Overview: I am a day trader who trades EURUSD from 02:00-05:00 EST. I need a machine learning algorithm to execute as well as optimize a 1:3 risk/reward trade based on a specific breakout strategy.

Trading Strategy Details:

Find the Price Range:

Look at the price changes of EURUSD from 20:00 to 00:00 EST.

Find the highest price (high) and the lowest price (low) during this time.

Look for a Breakout:

After 02:00 EST, keep watching the price for market profile and trade setup.

A breakout happens if the price goes above the high or below the low from the 20:00-00:00 EST range.

Best Time to Trade:

When a breakout happens, decide the best time to enter a trade.

Use different strategies (profiles) to find the best times to trade:

Momentum: Trade when the price is moving quickly in the breakout direction.

Pullback: Wait for the price to come back a little towards the breakout point before trading.

Trend Confirmation: Trade when other indicators also say the breakout is real.

Risk and Reward:

For each trade, aim to make three times the amount you are risking (1:3 risk/reward ratio).

Set a stop loss at a price level where the trade will close automatically if the price moves against you. The stop loss should be 1/3 of the amount you hope to gain.

Technical Needs:

Collect Data:

Get historical price data for EURUSD, focusing on the times mentioned.

Create Features:

Make features to find the high and low prices between 20:00-00:00 EST.

Use indicators to detect breakouts and find the best entry points using the profiles.

Train the Model:

Train a machine learning model to predict the best times to trade after a breakout.

Ensure the model can check the 1:3 risk/reward ratio and set stop losses correctly.

Backtest:

Test the strategy on past data to see how well it works.

Improve the model to make it more accurate and profitable.

Deploy:

Create the trading bot to work in real-time between 02:00-05:00 EST.

Make sure the bot can automatically make trades based on the model's predictions.

Goal:

A reliable machine learning trading algorithm that can find, act, and optimize breakout trades on the EURUSD market, aiming for a 1:3 risk/reward ratio with precise stop-loss settings.
